## Atmospheric CO~2~ varies across geologic time
<hr>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:15px; WIDTH:545px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/co2_atmos.png">

<div style="float: right; width: 48%;">

* **CO~2~ ranged 180 - 4000 ppm in last 500 million years**

<br/>

* **The photorespiration problem was not as bad 500mya when life comes on to land**
    + the drawdown of CO~2~ starting when land plants evolve is pretty clear

<br/>

* **Large decline in CO~2~ last 30 million years**

<br/>

* **O~2~ levels started increasing (from 10%) starting 500 mya**
    + What does this mean for the current efficiency of C3 photosynthesis?

## New photosynthetic pathways evolved recently (~30 mya)
<hr>
<br/>

* **Rubisco has existed for billions of years**
    + evolved when O~2~ was negligible in the atmosphere
    + mutations have yet to produce a superior version of the enzyme for the environment to select

<br/>

* **Plants can do nothing about CO~2~ nor 0~2~ concentrations in the air**

<br/>

* **C3 plants keep stomata open during the data, allowing gas exchange, while losing H~2~0**
    + balance of CO~2~ in, H~2~O out is poor due to rubisco

<br/>

**Alternative solution 1: Compartmentalize rubisco and concentrate CO~2~**
<br/>
**Alternate solution 2: Open stomata at night when evaporative water loss is lower**

</div>

## Evolution of C4 photosynthesis
<hr>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:25px; WIDTH:550px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/c4cell.jpg">

<div style="float: right; width: 45%;">

* **Calvin cycle moved to *Bundle Sheath Cells* surrounding leaf veins**
    * some chloroplasts moved inside bundle sheath cells
    * **Brainstorm**: How/When would mutations/genes be involved?

<br/>

* **BSC cells are less permeable to gases**
    * what does this mean for photorespiration?

<br/>

* **Ring cell arrangement = Kranz Anatomy**
    + bundle sheath cells surround veins
    + mesophyll cells surround bundle sheath cells
</div>

## C4 plants concentrate CO~2~ around Rubisco *spatially*
<hr>

<div style="float: right; width: 65%;">

* **New C4 pathway separates Calvin cycle from high O~2~**

<br/>

* **C4 pathway: New enzyme, phosphoenolpyruvate carboxlylase (PEPC) fixes CO~2~ to PEP (0 affinity for O~2~) to make malate (4C)**
    + C4 pathway occurs in mesophyll cell chloroplasts
    + malate sent to bundle sheath cells via plasmodesmata

<br/>

* **Malate broken down to release CO~2~ inside bundle sheath cells**
    + C3 pathway in bundle sheath cell chloroplasts
    + Calvin cycle (C3) runs with only CO~2 present

<br/>

* **Hyper efficient with use of CO~2~**
    * BRAINSTORM: How does this impact stomatal behavior?

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:20px; WIDTH:350px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/c4.jpg">

## C4 is a turbo-charged form of photosynthesis
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

* **Most productive C4 plants have rates ~50% higher than C3 plants**
    + C4 evolved independently ~70 times

<br/>
    
* **~435,000 plant species, only *2%* are C4**
    + 3 of top 10 crop plants are C4
    + extremely rare in trees (1 family)
    
<br/>

* **C4 plants still account for 25% of productivity**
    
</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/c4_super.png">

## Why is C4 photosynthesis not dominant?
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 50%;">

* **Regeneration of PEP expensive (ATP)**
    + in addition to ATP needed for Calvin cycle
 
<br/>
 
* **Where is needed ATP generated?**
    + high light requirements also means hotter/drier

<br/>

* **Where should C4 plants live??**
    + efficiency vs dehydration for stomata
    + should be able to outcompete C3 plants

## Why are there virtually no C4 trees?
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">

* **Is it difficult for trees to transition from C4&rarr;C4?**
    + long generation times

<br/>

* **Why do C4 shrubs not evolve into C4 trees?**
    + they should have improved growth...

<br/>

* **Was shade a problem?**
    + some Hawaiian C4 trees live in understory

<br/>

* **C4 plants seem to have an issue growing tall**
    + ATP requirements of larger plants...

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:250px; LEFT:525px; WIDTH:525px; HEIGHT:300px" SRC="images/hawaii_trees.png">

## Why C4 matters to you: Water-use-efficiency
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 58%;">

* **Climate change impacts photosynthesis:**
    + &uarr; CO~2~
    + &uarr; temperatures
    + variable precipitation
    + variations in humidity

<br/>

* **C4 plants can make the same amount of sugars as C3, with less water usage**
    + *more CO~2~ assimilated per molecule of water loss*
    + ability to keep stomata closed more often
    
<br/>

* **C3 & C4 plants should both benefit from extra CO~2~**
    + only works in C3 if enough H~2~0

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:225px; LEFT:645px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/cica.gif">

## Evolution of CAM photosynthesis (C4 pathway w/out BSC)
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 42%;">

**Crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM) is an adatpation that improves conservation of water while still allowing photosynthesis**

<br/>

**Metabolic pathway almost identical to C4 pathway but without structural modifications**

<br/>

**Malate created from PEP and CO~2~, simply allowed to accumulate**

<br/>

**Difference is with stomatal behavior**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:175px; LEFT:5px; WIDTH:600px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/cam2.png">

## CAM concentrates CO~2~ around Rubisco *temporally*
<hr>

<div style="float: right; width: 52%;">

* **Stomata open at night only**
    + malate produced in large quantities
        + CO~2~ (stomata) + PEP
    + malate stored when Rubisco is inactive

<br/>

* **C4 vs CAM = substitute function of bundle sheath cell (C4) for "night shift"**
 
 <br/>
 
* **Calvin cycle needs ATP, NADPH from light reactions but they are not stable enough to be stored for 'night shift'**


<br/>

* **Stomata close during day (no CO~2~, O~2~ in) but stored malate (night shift) is broken down to release CO~2~**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:225px; LEFT:25px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/cam5.jpg">

## Yes we CAM!!
<hr>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:650px; WIDTH:300px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/cam_plants.jpeg">


<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">
* **CAM evolved independently several times**
    + ~16,000 species

<br/>

* **Exist in arid environments or habitats**
    * cacti
    * epiphytes

<br/>

* **CAM is not very efficient, released CO~2~ is used up within first few hours of daylight**
    + survival (harsher environments) over productivity

<br/>

* **Are CAM plants fast or slow growing?**
<br/>
* **Should CAM plants have many or few stomata?**
</div>
